description: Electricity tariffs and providers in Germany for the user's postal code (Postleitzahl): estimated price per kWh, monthly base fee and yearly cost for the cheapest fixed-price offer, certified green power, a dynamic hourly tariff (from today's live EPEX day-ahead prices, via Energy-Charts or aWATTar, no key) and the local default supply (Grundversorgung), built from the state's grid fee, the town's concession fee, the 2026 levies, electricity tax and VAT. Names providers for each type, the local default supplier for large cities, the cheapest hours ahead on the exchange, heat-pump (§14a) and electric-car options, and what the user saves against their current tariff. Use it when the user asks which electricity provider or tariff to pick in Germany, what power should cost where they live, whether to switch, or whether a dynamic tariff pays off. It needs a location: if the user hasn't said where they live, don't guess and don't call it yet. First ask with ask_user for their 5-digit postal code (an open question), and in the same call, if they haven't said, their yearly use in kWh from the bill or household size (options 1, 2, 3, 4, 5+ people). Then call with postal_code and annual_kwh or household_size, plus current_price_ct and current_base_eur_month if they know their current tariff. Turn the result into a short answer: lead with the cheapest sensible option and its yearly cost, then what it saves against default supply or their current tariff, then whether a dynamic tariff suits them. Say the figures are estimates from public price components, not offers: exact prices for their address come from the linked comparison sites or providers. Never present a provider's price as quoted. Its output ends with [chart] lines, which the chat draws for the user (yearly cost per option, and the dynamic price by hour): don't repeat every number or redraw them with generate_chart unless the user asks for an image file.
author: Hannes Hapke

postal_code.description: The user's 5-digit German postal code, such as "10115". Ask with ask_user when you don't have it.

location.description: Instead of postal_code: a German town or city, such as "Leipzig". Less precise.

annual_kwh.description: Yearly household use in kWh, from the last bill. Without it, household_size estimates it.

household_size.description: People in the household, to estimate annual_kwh when it isn't known.

green_only.description: Only show green power and dynamic options.

heat_pump.description: The household has or plans a heat pump: adds a heat-pump tariff on its own meter (§14a EnWG).

heat_pump_kwh.description: The heat pump's yearly use in kWh, if known (default 4500).

ev.description: The household charges an electric car at home: adds its typical use to an estimated annual_kwh and car tariff tips.

current_provider.description: The user's current supplier, to name it in the comparison.

current_price_ct.description: The user's current price per kWh in cents, gross (Arbeitspreis brutto).

current_base_eur_month.description: The user's current monthly base fee in euros, gross (Grundpreis brutto).

grid_fee_ct.description: The local grid fee in ct/kWh net, if the user knows it from their grid operator's price sheet; replaces the state average.
